documents.title: Translate text and speech input
documents.excerpt: Translation has two public paths: a private one-off translation and an optional before-speaking preference. Automatic channel mappings are server controls.
documents.text: ADDITIONAL TOOLS Translate text and speech input Translation has two public paths: a private one-off translation and an optional before-speaking preference. Automatic channel mappings are server controls. PRIVATE TEXT Translate without posting a public result /translate text text:Olá locale:en This command sends the translation only to you. Use /translate language to save your usual language. OPTIONAL SPEAKING PATH Translate before Vozen speaks /translate speak-language locale:en enables the preference; use locale:off to disable it. If the service is unavailable, Vozen safely reads the original text instead of inventing a translation. Members can use /translate opt-out to opt out of configured automatic translations. Administrators can inspect or manage mappings with status , enable , disable , clear , map-add , map-remove , map-list and preview . Translation is opt-in where it changes speech. documents.text: GETTING STARTED Install Vozen TTS The public install flow is designed to end in a working, explainable setup instead of a long settings tour. 01 · Add the app Use the public Vozen invite and select a server where you can manage the server. 02 · Review access Keep the permissions Discord shows in the install screen, then review channel overrides. 03 · Run setup Use /setup ; optionally choose a text channel and a short voice check. 04 · Join voice Enter a voice channel and run /join . 05 · Test once Send a small message or run /tts before inviting everyone into the flow. FIRST COMMAND /setup is the starting point /setup accepts an optional text channel and an optional test voice. If the channel is omitted, the current text channel is used. Vozen checks the text-channel and voice-channel permissions it can verify, then reports any missing item. /setup channel:#lounge test-voice:true Never paste secrets into setup. Vozen’s public installation needs Discord’s app flow, not a bot token, guild ID or private configuration file. RECOVERY If the setup report is incomplete Fix the marked permission on Vozen’s role or on the channel override, then run /setup again. The setup message is safe to repeat. It does not require a private dashboard route.

documents.title: Meet Vozen TTS
documents.excerpt: Vozen turns readable Discord messages into ordered voice output. Members can choose their own voice; administrators control the server channel, defaults and limits.
documents.text: GETTING STARTED Meet Vozen TTS Vozen turns readable Discord messages into ordered voice output. Members can choose their own voice; administrators control the server channel, defaults and limits. WHAT IT DOES One voice path, several controls The core flow is intentionally small: join a voice channel, connect Vozen, choose where text comes from, and let the queue handle playback. Personal voice preferences do not replace the server’s safety controls. Auto-read can be tied to one text channel. /tts reads a single text immediately. Personal voices, speeds, engines and effects can be changed without changing another member’s voice. Private tools such as /tts-file and /translate text do not require Vozen to join a call. The free path is complete. Piper voices, the core auto-read flow and the administrative controls are part of the free core. Premium adds optional engines and higher-cost extras. documents.title: Privacy and data controls
documents.excerpt: Vozen keeps the public voice path bounded: messages are processed for speech, private audio files are not stored after delivery, and live transcription requires consent.
documents.text: PRIVACY AND SERVICE HEALTH Privacy and data controls Vozen keeps the public voice path bounded: messages are processed for speech, private audio files are not stored after delivery, and live transcription requires consent. PERSONAL ERASURE /privacy erase The confirmation flow deletes erasable personal data across servers, including voice settings, spoken nickname, personal pronunciations, birthday, game scores, talk statistics and opt-out state. It cannot be undone. Paid Premium/Plus and the purchase history required for financial records are retained. Erasure is not a payment cancellation. CONTENT BOUNDARIES Know where a result lives /tts-file returns a private attachment and the current Vozen list says it is not stored after delivery. Queue views expose metadata, not a public transcript of every message. Live transcription posts messages to Discord. Revoke consent stops future transcription for that member; it does not delete messages already posted. Translation mappings and preferences are server/member configuration, not a public command log. Use Discord for Discord content deletion. If a transcript message is already in a channel, delete it there according to the server’s moderation and retention policy.

documents.title: Spoken variables and output
documents.excerpt: Vozen does not publish a general-purpose message template language for TTS. Vozen owns the final spoken text and protects Discord mentions while preparing it.
documents.text: REFERENCE Spoken variables and output Vozen does not publish a general-purpose message template language for TTS. Vozen owns the final spoken text and protects Discord mentions while preparing it. SPEAKER ANNOUNCEMENT {name} is an output marker When /config x-said is enabled, the public current Vozen list describes the spoken shape as “{name} said …”. The name comes from the member’s display context or their /voice nickname ; it is not a free-form server template. PRONUNCIATION Replace speech, not messages Personal and server pronunciation rules transform the spoken form of a matching term. The original Discord message stays as written, and the rule scope remains personal or server-wide. No private placeholders. Do not publish tokens, IDs, internal interpolation keys or owner-only output names as if they were public variables.

documents.text: SERVER CONFIGURATION Set limits and role gates Limits are part of the voice experience: they keep a busy channel usable and make expensive or disruptive behaviour visible. Control Public range or behaviour /config max-chars 1–2000 characters per message. /config rate-limit 1–120 messages per minute per user. /config role Only members with the selected role are read. /config priority-role Give an accessibility queue priority role. /config blocked-role Prevent a role from adding audio to the queue. /config block-word Manage the server blocklist. /config anti-spam Ignore repeated or oversized spam patterns when enabled. RECOVERY Change one bound at a time Start with the character cap or rate limit, observe the queue, then add a role gate only if the server needs it. documents.title: Understand the queue
documents.excerpt: Vozen queues audio, not a public transcript. Queue views expose only the metadata needed to manage playback.
documents.text: TEXT TO SPEECH Understand the queue Vozen queues audio, not a public transcript. Queue views expose only the metadata needed to manage playback. QUEUE CONTROLS Member and administrator actions Command Who can use it Effect /queue show Members Show pending queue metadata. /queue remove Member or administrator Remove one queued item; administrators may remove any item. /queue clear Manage Server Clear queued audio. /queue skip Manage Server Skip the current item. /queue pause Manage Server Pause playback. /queue resume Manage Server Resume playback. /skip Members Skip the current audio item. /shut-up Members Clear the whole queue immediately. RECOVERY Keep playback predictable Use /queue show to inspect the state, then remove or skip the smallest item that is blocking progress. Use /shut-up when the correct action is immediate silence, not a re-ordered queue.

documents.title: Read messages
documents.excerpt: Auto-read is a server choice. Personal voice settings change how a member sounds, not which channels the server allows.
documents.text: TEXT TO SPEECH Read messages Auto-read is a server choice. Personal voice settings change how a member sounds, not which channels the server allows. AUTO-READ Choose a text source Use /setup for the guided path or /config tts-channel to change the channel later. Auto-read is off until the server enables it. /config tts-channel channel:#lounge\n/config auto-read active:true SPEAKER CONTEXT Make the voice traceable /config x-said active:true adds a spoken “name said” lead-in. A member can set a spoken nickname with /voice nickname . Bots and webhooks are ignored by default; administrators can opt in with /config read-bots active:true . Wrong channel Check the configured TTS channel and its View Channel permission. Unexpected bot messages Review the read-bots toggle and channel sources. Too much output Use a character cap, rate limit, blocked role or anti-spam.

documents.text: TROUBLESHOOTING Vozen does not join The join path needs a member in a voice channel and Connect permission for Vozen in that channel. 01 · Context Join the voice channel you want to use. 02 · Command Run /join . 03 · Check Read the response for the exact missing Connect or Speak permission. 04 · Fix Update the role or channel overwrite. 05 · Retry Run /join again, then use /tts . No voice context The member who runs /join must be in a voice channel. Connect missing Grant Connect to Vozen in that voice channel. Speak missing Grant Speak or remove a conflicting channel overwrite.

Game How it works Guess the Language I read a sentence in a random language — first to name it wins the point. Mental Math I say a sum out loud — first to type the answer wins. Missing Number I count out loud but skip one number — first to catch it wins. Spelling Bee I say a word — first to spell it correctly wins. Funny Accent I say a word with a foreign accent — first to write it wins. Reflexes I count down, then shout GO — first to type after that wins. Don't jump early! documents.title: Start and stop a game
documents.excerpt: A game needs a voice session and a free game slot on the server.
documents.text: VOICE GAMES Start and stop a game A game needs a voice session and a free game slot on the server. 01 · Join voice Run /join before starting a voice game. 02 · Pick a game Use /game play or inspect the list first. 03 · Play the round Vozen reads prompts and members answer in the text channel. 04 · Stop early Use /game stop when the current round should end. 05 · Review Use /game leaderboard or /game stats . GUARDRAILS One active game per server path Vozen reports when another game is already active, when there are not enough players, or when the selected game has no current voice-language data. A stop action ends the game; it does not erase historical scores. Not in voice Join a voice channel and run /join . Game already active Finish it or run /game stop .
